headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon
dek: The cyber-focused model starts with restricted access for defense teams, per DeepMind.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Google's strongest model
body: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Carbon, which it calls its strongest model, built around cybersecurity work.
Per DeepMind, access starts this week, but only for a restricted group of cyber defense teams.

points.t: 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, finding flaws (Google DeepMind).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Long jobs and pricing
body: DeepMind says Carbon was built for long engineering problems and ran for days at a stretch in tests.
Launch pricing matches Gemini 4 Argon, per Google DeepMind: $2 per million input tokens.

items.t: Trusted partners via the Fairwind Program (DeepMind).
No date yet for developers or consumers.

caption.hook: Google DeepMind launched Gemini 4 Carbon, a cybersecurity-focused model with access limited to defense teams.
body: Per DeepMind, Carbon tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59 and hit 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, a test of finding flaws in code. Those figures come from the company, not an independent measurement.

DeepMind says the model was built for long engineering tasks and keeps the launch price of Gemini 4 Argon, $2 per million input tokens. Access starts with cyber defenders and then reaches Fairwind Program partners, with no date for the general public.
caption.cta: Should powerful cyber models stay restricted at first?
